def: A family of search algorithms that return many different solutions, each as good as possible for its kind of behaviour, instead of one best solution.
A quality-diversity algorithm that keeps the best solution found in each cell of a grid over behaviour space and mutates randomly chosen elites.
A short vector, chosen by the designer, describing what a solution does, used to decide which archive cell it belongs to.
The space of all possible behaviour descriptor values, in which nearby points mean similar behaviour.
The data structure holding one best solution per region of behaviour space, which is the output of a quality-diversity run.
The best solution found so far for one cell of an archive.
The fraction of archive cells that hold a solution, showing how much of behaviour space has been explored.
The sum of the qualities of all elites in an archive, which rises when cells are filled or improved.
Using search to show how performance varies across behaviour space, rather than only finding the single best point.
A MAP-Elites variant that divides behaviour space into a fixed number of centroidal Voronoi regions so high-dimensional descriptors stay tractable.
A quality-diversity method that selects for behavioural novelty while letting each solution compete on fitness only against its behavioural neighbours.
Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback: a method where a language model proposes variations and judges quality and diversity of the candidates.
